1 أَلَقَ , (JK, K, TA,) aor.
اَلِقَ ; (K, TA;) or أَلِقَ, aor.
اَلَقَ ; (CK; [in which it would seem, from what follows in this paragraph and the next, that the pret. is wrong, but that the aor. is right;]) inf. n. أَلْقٌ and إِلَاقٌ; (JK, K;) It (lightning) lied; (AHeyth, K;) [i. e.] it was without rain. (JK.) ―
-b2- See also 5. ―
-b3- Also, أَلَقَ, aor.
اَلَقَ , inf. n. أَلْقٌ, He lied; spoke falsely: whence the reading of Aboo-Jaafar and Zeyd Ibn-Aslam, [in the Kur xxiv. 14,] إِذْ تَأْلَقُونَهُ تألّق [When ye spoke it falsely with your tongues]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
